body:
Minutes:

- Proposal to Extend Window Open to Split Tabs: Mason Freed presented issue 13153, a proposal to give developers access to browser split tab features through two mechanisms: a new `split` value for `window.open` or window features, and a declarative `windowfeatures` attribute for links ([00:04:16](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.ebx83sa24a4m)). Regarding edge cases where an app is already split, Mason Freed explained that requests fall back to opening a new tab. Discussions involving Mason Freed, Olli Pettay, Emilio Cobos Álvarez, and Robert Flack addressed feature detection, privacy fingerprinting concerns, and navigation behavior for multiple links ([00:08:32](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.9yhiklx2hnkd)) ([00:17:49](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.k01eaayt3abk)). Jacques Newman also raised questions about supporting more than two split tabs on ultra-wide monitors, to which Mason Freed responded that the specification could theoretically support it ([00:14:58](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.cny5y2po8rvv)). Olli Pettay expressed support for moving the proposal to stage one, and Johnny Stenback agreed to add the stage one label ([00:18:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.pnz48t1044t8)).
- HTML Image Preview API Proposal: Olga Gerchikov presented issue 13176, an HTML image preview API designed to provide temporary content while main images load without requiring custom scripts or extra element layering ([00:18:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.pnz48t1044t8)). The proposal allows browsers to consume typed preview data, including URLs, self-contained CSS colors, and compact representations ([00:21:23](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.7ev8w7pxfmnm)). Robert Flack questioned the necessity of separate resolution versions and expressed concerns that separate preview fetches might delay real images and that progressive images are superior ([00:23:58](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.13kcfsvo5swd)). Alex Russell and Olga Gerchikov argued that previews offer scheduling benefits by avoiding heavyweight image fetches that block page bandwidth, noting that inline data URLs and compact formats like blur hash are the primary intended use cases ([00:26:28](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.q8y2f0jvm6z9)).
- Architectural Discussion on HTML Image Previews: Emilio Cobos Álvarez and Noam Rosenthal raised architectural concerns, arguing that image previews should ideally be implemented as CSS features rather than HTML attributes to prevent historical issues like layout and transparency mismatches reminiscent of 1990s low source attributes ([00:28:18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.l53pftr0k04a)) ([00:32:04](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.wddwxloh0rpt)). Alex Russell agreed to explore alternative CSS-based presentations for comparison ([00:33:47](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.en7t5xcf42kf)). Additionally, Emilio Cobos Álvarez discussed interactions with lazy loading (`loading="lazy"`), pointing out that previews should not inappropriately block the load event, a detail Alex Russell acknowledged as a helpful point for standardizing load event behavior ([00:35:55](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.lfim0kw0z8m4)) ([00:38:27](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.yr47dtxvih1s)).
- AsyncContext Proposal Integration and Stage Two Status: Nicolò Ribaudo provided an update on issue 10432 regarding the HTML and web specifications integration of the AsyncContext proposal, noting that DOM integration work was complete except for minor fixes related to data signal timeouts. Nicolò Ribaudo requested stage two approval. However, Olli Pettay stated they had not yet reviewed the most recent pull requests and requested two weeks to read them ([00:40:18](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.70c9imw83in4)). Nicolò Ribaudo agreed to return in two weeks to seek stage two approval once Olli Pettay finished reviewing the documentation ([00:41:37](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.k6o82ml42145)).
- Mutation Observer Batch Delivery Proposal: Noam Rosenthal presented issue 13198, a proposal to allow mutation observer batch delivery by adding a delivery initialization option (`stream` or `batch`) and an `is streaming` boolean to handle custom element streams efficiently ([00:42:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.uyx8npbk9utc)). Olli Pettay strongly criticized the scheduling changes, arguing they deviate from standard microtask scheduling and introduce complications with script elements and mid-parse modifications. Anne van Kesteren questioned batching boundaries and timing consistency alongside Noam Rosenthal ([00:47:53](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.u0djce1nsgw3)) ([00:51:21](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.i9rfx2gid0jv)). While concerns regarding scheduling remained, Olli Pettay noted that some form of end-of-tag observation mechanism is needed, and Noam Rosenthal indicated willingness to refine the design ([00:50:12](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.iurm4f7tpn7f)) ([00:54:28](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.cz92vxxpnkxh)). There was in the end agreement that Stage 1 made sense for this work.
- Meeting Schedule Adjustments for US Holidays: David Baron highlighted schedule disruptions caused by upcoming US holidays, noting that the next US-friendly time slot lands on US Thanksgiving. Johnny Stenback and David Baron proposed swapping the schedule alternation between Thanksgiving and Christmas so participants in the US have more attending sessions, while canceling meetings on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve ([00:55:21](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.ndybkkm200y0)). Mason Freed voted in favor of implementing the swap starting the following week. Johnny Stenback confirmed that the schedule will be adjusted accordingly ([00:56:38](https://docs.google.com/document/d/14WBSxQP4fTSSZEqy5p_mZbvikx_z2EChtQ3f9YyExBY/edit?sharingaction=manageaccess&tab=t.8ny4k78eft2f#heading=h.yo8jqo4whek5)).
